plan.planning_summary: This portfolio tests three distinct design axes for a long-pass dichroic coating that transmits 1000-1700 nm SWIR while reflecting 300-450 nm UV/blue. Route 1 tests a classical periodic quarter-wave stack where the hypothesis is that regular alternation suffices. Route 2 tests a chirped/depth-graded stack where thickness varies through the stack to broaden the reflection band. Route 3 tests a fully non-periodic optimized stack where no structural assumption constrains the search. These axes are genuinely distinct: if periodicity matters, Route 1 and Route 3 will disagree; if bandwidth broadening via grading helps, Route 2 will outperform Route 1. All routes use only HfO2 and SiO2 on fused silica substrate with maximum 30 layers, preserving the user's material and manufacturing constraints.

routes.title: Periodic Quarter-Wave Stack for UV Reflection with SWIR Transmission
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A periodic alternating stack of HfO2 and SiO2 quarter-wave layers tuned for the UV reflection band can achieve high reflectance in 300-450 nm while maintaining high transmittance in 1000-1700 nm without requiring thickness grading or non-periodic optimization.
routes.design_principle: Bragg reflection from periodic dielectric stacks creates high reflectance bands centered at the design wavelength. By setting the quarter-wave condition at the UV band center (~375 nm), the stack reflects UV while the SWIR band falls outside the reflection band and transmits through.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | (HfO2 | SiO2) repeated 12 times | Fused Silica substrate
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for each of the 24 layers
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
maximize mean reflectance in 300-450 nm band
minimize layer count while meeting performance targets
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 24 (within 30-layer limit)
all layers must be physically realizable thicknesses (10-500 nm range)
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard ion-beam deposition materials
theory_basis: Transfer matrix method for multilayer dielectric coatings
Refractive index contrast between HfO2 (~2.0) and SiO2 (~1.45) determines reflection bandwidth
expected_advantages: L01 and L04 demonstrate dichroic coatings using similar periodic approaches
known_risks: Periodic stacks have limited reflection bandwidth; 300-450 nm is 50% bandwidth which may exceed single periodic stack capability
SWIR transmission may suffer from higher-order reflection bands
L27 notes that periodic designs may not reach global optimum
routes.execution_request_english: Design a periodic multilayer dielectric coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees. The stack consists of 24 layers: alternating HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) layers, starting with HfO2 adjacent to air. Optimize all 24 individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 1000-1700 nm wavelength band while maximizing reflectance in 300-450 nm wavelength band. Total layer count is exactly 24. Materials are HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) only. Evaluate performance using transfer matrix method across both wavelength bands.

routes.title: Chirped Depth-Graded Stack for Broadened UV Reflection Band
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A depth-graded stack where bilayer thickness increases from air toward substrate will broaden the UV reflection band beyond what a periodic stack achieves, while maintaining SWIR transmission by keeping longer-period layers deeper in the stack.
routes.design_principle: Depth-graded multilayers (L24) use varying bilayer thickness to create constructive interference across a broader wavelength range. Thinner bilayers near the air interface reflect shorter wavelengths; thicker bilayers deeper in the stack reflect longer wavelengths within the UV band, collectively broadening the reflection band.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | 15 bilayers of (HfO2 | SiO2) with thickness increasing from air to substrate | Fused Silica substrate
design_variables: bilayer thickness gradient parameter (rate of thickness increase per bilayer)
base bilayer thickness at air interface
maximum bilayer thickness at substrate interface
soft_objectives: maximize mean reflectance across full 300-450 nm band (not just center)
maintain mean transmittance above 90% in 1000-1700 nm band
minimize thickness gradient to reduce fabrication complexity
manufacturing_considerations: thickness gradient must be monotonic for fabrication reproducibility
L08 demonstrates HfO2 deposition control in multilayer structures
theory_basis: Depth-graded multilayer theory for broadband reflection (L24)
L39 demonstrates wideband dichroic coating fabrication using graded approaches
expected_advantages: Broader reflection bandwidth than periodic stack
L24 shows depth-graded coatings achieve high reflectivity across wide spectral ranges
Better tolerance to wavelength shift from angle variation
known_risks: Graded stacks require more precise thickness control during deposition
May introduce more absorption if HfO2 layers become too thick
L26 notes defect formation in HfO2 films can affect optical properties
routes.execution_request_english: Design a chirped multilayer dielectric coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees. The stack consists of 30 layers: 15 bilayers of alternating HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand), starting with HfO2 adjacent to air. Bilayer thickness increases monotonically from air interface to substrate interface. Optimize three parameters: base bilayer thickness at air side, thickness increment per bilayer, and maximum bilayer thickness at substrate side. Maximize reflectance in 300-450 nm band while maximizing transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band. Total layer count is exactly 30. Materials are HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) only.

routes.title: Non-Periodic Globally Optimized Stack Without Structural Assumptions
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Removing periodicity and grading constraints allows the optimizer to find layer thickness combinations that periodic or chirped stacks cannot achieve, potentially discovering non-intuitive thickness sequences that better separate the UV reflection and SWIR transmission bands.
routes.design_principle: Global optimization (L27) explores the full parameter space without structural priors. The optimizer may discover that certain layers should be thicker or thinner than quarter-wave, or that specific layer sequences break symmetry to improve performance in ways periodic designs cannot.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | 28 layers of alternating HfO2 and SiO2 with individually optimized thicknesses | Fused Silica substrate
design_variables: all 28 individual layer thicknesses as independent variables
layer sequence order (which material starts at air interface)
soft_objectives: maximize combined score of UV reflectance and SWIR transmittance
discover if non-periodic thickness patterns outperform structured approaches
identify which layers are most sensitive to thickness variation
manufacturing_considerations: 28 layers within 30-layer limit, leaving margin for possible capping layer
no thickness constraints beyond physical realizability (5-400 nm per layer)
L27 notes global optimization can find designs tolerant to fabrication errors
theory_basis: Genetic algorithm optimization for thin-film stacks (L21)

expected_advantages: No structural assumptions limit the search space

routes.execution_request_english: Design a non-periodic multilayer dielectric coating on fused silica substrate with air incidence at 0 degrees. The stack consists of 28 layers: alternating HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) starting with HfO2 adjacent to air. All 28 layer thicknesses are independent optimization variables with no periodicity or gradient constraints. Optimize all thicknesses simultaneously to maximize transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Total layer count is exactly 28. Materials are HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) only. Use global optimization algorithm to explore full parameter space.

plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all three routes fail to achieve best_target_score above 0.7 after full optimization, the HfO2/SiO2 material pair may be fundamentally insufficient for the 300-450 nm reflection bandwidth requirement; consider expanding material catalogue or relaxing bandwidth specifications.

expected_observations: If the periodic hypothesis holds, best_target_score should increase with optimization rounds and stabilize as thicknesses converge to quarter-wave values near 375 nm center wavelength
If the periodic hypothesis fails, best_target_score will plateau below acceptable levels and tightest_margin will not improve across rounds, indicating bandwidth limitation
valid_candidates should remain high (above 10 per round) if the design space is well-conditioned
thicknesses_nm should converge to values near 90-100 nm for HfO2 and 130-140 nm for SiO2 if quarter-wave condition at 375 nm is optimal
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If valid_candidates falls below 5 for three consecutive rounds, relax thickness bounds and continue for one more round before stopping

expected_observations: If the chirped hypothesis holds, best_target_score should show higher final values than route_01 and tightest_margin should remain stable or improve across rounds
If the chirped hypothesis fails, best_target_score will not exceed route_01's performance and thickness gradient parameters will converge to near-zero (effectively becoming periodic)
valid_candidates should remain above 8 per round if the gradient parameterization is well-posed
thicknesses_nm should show monotonic increase from air to substrate if the chirped structure is optimal
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
If the optimized thickness gradient converges to less than 1 nm per bilayer, the chirped advantage is not realized; stop and flag this axis as not beneficial over periodic

expected_observations: If the non-periodic hypothesis holds, best_target_score should exceed both route_01 and route_02, and thicknesses_nm should show no periodic or monotonic pattern
If the non-periodic hypothesis fails, best_target_score will converge to values similar to route_01 and thicknesses_nm will self-organize into near-periodic patterns despite no constraint
valid_candidates may be lower (5-10 per round) due to higher-dimensional search space
tightest_margin should not decrease across rounds if the optimizer finds robust solutions
stop_conditions: If best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
